issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the feeding method using two different names: the UML and several tasks require an abstract method messageOnFeed(), but other places (e.g., the instructions for feedAllAnimals() and per-animal descriptions) refer to getFeedingSound(). The solution and UML use messageOnFeed(). This naming inconsistency can confuse students about which method to implement and which name to call from Farm.feedAllAnimals() and singFarmSongVerse().
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the method name across the problem statement and templates. Replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem text with messageOnFeed() (or explicitly state that getFeedingSound() is an alias for messageOnFeed()). Ensure the Farm description and per-animal instructions consistently reference messageOnFeed() so students know which method to implement and call.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to a method named getFeedingSound() for animals in multiple places, while the provided solution (and the UML) use the method name messageOnFeed(). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (the animal feeding sound) can confuse students when mapping the textual requirements to the code they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the method name across artifacts. Update problem_statement.md to refer to messageOnFeed() where it currently mentions getFeedingSound(), or alternatively change the code to provide a getFeedingSound() method that delegates to messageOnFeed(). Prefer keeping messageOnFeed() (as in the UML and solution) and edit the problem text to match.
